beats: Start with the unit circle and a point P on it, at angle θ.
Halfway from 1 to P is B. The circle at 1 through B has radius sin(θ/2): that is k.
p = 0: a circle the same size, at P, touches it. Copies keep going around the unit circle, and the ring closes when θ = 360°/q.
Its other two neighbors sit on the ray halfway to P, one inside the unit circle and one outside.
Mirror them across the real axis: six circles around one, and every circle the same ratio k to its distance from 0.
q = 2p: the circle about −½ through cos(θ/2) crosses the unit circle at F. The next neighbors lie in that direction.
Two neighbors on that ray, touching the circle at 1 where the ray halfway to F crosses it.
And two on the real axis, the direction that is a pure zoom. Each touches its neighbor where that same ray crosses it again.
Mirror the pair across the real axis: the q = 2p flower.
Every center in both flowers lies on one curve, the level curve of the circle at 1. One way to draw it: the pedal of the circle on the two real-axis centers, seen from 1.
